title: Let your phone nap in another room
description: Your phone does not need to be off or locked away forever. It just needs to not be on the desk while you are trying to think.

body.heading: Presence is the problem
paragraphs: A phone face-down on the desk still makes quiet demands: the urge to check, the half-heard buzz, the thought of what might be happening elsewhere. Many people find their focus improves simply when the phone is physically elsewhere.
This is not about discipline. It is about distance. Willpower is a fair fight against a craving; it is an unfair one against a glowing rectangle within arm's reach.

body.heading: Try the nap, notice the difference
paragraphs: For one work session, charge your phone in another room and tell anyone who might urgently need you how else to reach you. Then work, and pay attention to the first ten minutes, which are the itchiest.
Afterwards, compare honestly: how much did you get done, and how did it feel? Most people keep the habit in some form, not because a rule says so, but because the quieter sessions are simply nicer.

takeaway: Charge the phone in another room for one session, and enjoy the quieter mind.
